subdomain: 3.2 Analyze authentication and authorization requirements to identify security gaps

en.question: A protected HTTP MCP deployment implements the authorization specification for MCP 2026-07-28. An integrator assumes the authorization server must be hosted at the MCP endpoint's origin and rejects a separately hosted identity service. What discovery design should replace this assumption?

options.text: Use the MCP server's OAuth Protected Resource Metadata to discover its advertised authorization server.
options.note: This version requires the protected MCP resource to implement RFC 9728 metadata and the client to use it for authorization-server discovery. The authorization server can be hosted separately from the resource.

options.text: Try the user's existing identity-provider token against the MCP endpoint and infer the issuer from success.
options.note: A token for another resource is not a discovery mechanism and must not be accepted merely because its signature is valid. Discovery should precede requesting a token for the intended MCP resource.

options.text: Read the authorization-server URL from the description of the first tool returned by the server.
options.note: Tool descriptions are not the specified authorization discovery channel. A protected endpoint may require authorization before it returns tools at all.

options.text: Require Dynamic Client Registration at the MCP endpoint's origin before considering any other issuer.
options.note: Dynamic Client Registration is optional compatibility support in this version, not a mandatory same-origin bootstrap. Protected Resource Metadata supplies the required discovery boundary.
